extracted.intended_audience: medical journal peer reviewers and editors (reviewer-training audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist-style operational rubric for what peer reviewers (especially of medical randomized trials) should detect in manuscripts, derived from Schroter et al. 2008 error-insertion study. Focuses on major methodological faults and common minor reporting errors reviewers ought to spot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate / inappropriate randomisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Inadequate or inappropriate randomisation (e.g. alternation, day-of-week, biased allocation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify the randomisation procedure is described and free of bias; look for obvious non-random methods such as alternation or predictable schedules. Examples given: alternation, day-of-week allocation, or other biased allocation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing details of randomisation method (sequence generation not described)
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing details of randomisation method (sequence generation not described).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether sequence generation is explicitly described; absence of detail about how the random sequence was produced is a methodological flaw and should be queried.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing allocation concealment
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing allocation concealment (no description of how the random sequence was hidden).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify allocation concealment is described (how investigators enrolling participants were kept unaware of upcoming assignments). Lack of concealment or failure to report it increases risk of selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate exclusion of participants post-randomisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Inappropriate exclusion of participants post-randomisation (violation of intention-to-treat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that all randomised participants are accounted for and analysed in the group to which they were randomised; flag post-randomisation exclusions that bias results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to use intention-to-treat analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to use intention-to-treat analysis despite preserving randomisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the analysis preserves the benefits of randomisation (intention-to-treat). If participants are excluded or analysed per-protocol without justification, note risk of biased estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate statistical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Inappropriate statistical analysis (wrong test for the data type).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether statistical methods are appropriate for the data and study design; watch for use of incorrect tests, misuse of parametric methods, or analyses that do not match the stated outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrepancy between data shown and conclusion drawn
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrepancy between data shown and conclusion drawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the data presented in results, tables and figures support the narrative conclusions; identify mismatches where the text overstates or misinterprets the results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions not supported by the data
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions not supported by the data (overgeneralisation, claim beyond evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess concordance of conclusions with data in magnitude, direction and certainty; flag overgeneralisation, causal claims without basis, or claims exceeding the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate / overstated subgroup analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Inappropriate / overstated subgroup analysis (post-hoc, multiple comparisons not adjusted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish prespecified versus post-hoc subgroup analyses; discount or qualify findings from post-hoc analyses and check for lack of adjustment for multiple comparisons or fishing for significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inaccurate reporting of percentages in the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Inaccurate reporting of percentages in the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that percentages reported in the abstract match the numbers in the main text/tables; independently recompute summary statistics where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorrect total in a table
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check table totals for arithmetic errors and consistency with text; spot-check sums and recompute key totals if numbers appear inconsistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mismatch between text and figure caption
rubrics_metrics.description: Mismatch between text and figure caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure figures, their captions and any referenced values in the text are concordant; note any discrepancies between caption, figure content, and textual description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical errors in summary statistics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for typos in means, standard deviations, confidence intervals and p-values; independently verify summary statistics where possible (recompute from data reported).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorrect citation in the reference list / citation mismatch
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorrect citation in the reference list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spot-check at least one citation to ensure it says what the paper claims it says; verify reference details and that citations are correctly attributed.
